title: Probabilistic probe smoothing and multi-signal KEDA/HPA calibration — investigation and action plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-03 we observed an autoscaling regression that caused sustained under-provisioning of inference nodes during a regional traffic surge, resulting in elevated tail latencies and increased 5xx errors for ~18 minutes. This ticket documents the investigation into why HPA + KEDA did not bring capacity up fast enough, the findings that point to an aggregation/smoothing regression, and the concrete action items to prevent recurrence. The root of the problem was a recent change to the metric aggregation path (runtime-2.1.0) that reduced percentile smoothing and changed the default KEDA scaler sampling behavior; combined with higher variance in warm-start latencies this produced both false negatives (scale-up delayed) and false positives (premature scale-down), harming SLOs.
timeline: 2026-03-03T09:12Z - Pager fired: inference-p10 latency > SLO in us-east-1; automated on-call notified
2026-03-03T09:15Z - Ops runbook executed: verified increased queue depth and rising tail latency metrics
2026-03-03T09:18Z - Temporary mitigation: bumped HPA minReplicas from 10 to 14 for critical pool, scaled up warm-pool nodes manually
2026-03-03T09:30Z - KEDA scaler metrics review: redis-queue scaler reported noisy percentiles, many short spikes in sample window
2026-03-03T09:40Z - Reverted autoscaler aggregation config change in canary; canary showed smoother percentile curves and faster scale-up on synthetic load
2026-03-03T09:50Z - Production rollback of runtime-2.1.0 autoscaler aggregation change to restore previous EWMA smoothing behavior
2026-03-03T10:00Z - Latency returned to baseline; incident declared resolved at 10:12Z after monitoring confirmed stability
postmortem_summary: Root cause: an aggregation smoothing regression introduced in runtime-2.1.0 reduced the effective smoothing on percentile calculations used by both HPA and our KEDA Redis scaler. The change made recent samples weigh too heavily, amplifying short-lived spikes and noise. KEDA's scaler implementation also switched to a faster approxQuantile mode to reduce CPU, which increased variance for heavy-tailed distributions. Together these changes produced delayed scale-ups and premature scale-downs during bursty traffic with heavy tail latency variance. Impact: ~18 minutes of elevated tail latency; several customers observed higher per-request latencies and transient 5xx rate increases. Detection: alerted by latency SLO dashboard and on-call noise. Mitigation: temporary minReplica increase, warm-pool seeding, and immediate rollback of the aggregation change.
root_causes: Change: Reduced percentile aggregation smoothing in autoscaler aggregation module (commit: github.com/redwood/inference@a1b2c3d)
Change: KEDA Redis scaler switched to approximate quantile mode to cut CPU; this increased variance for tail metrics
Operational: no multi-signal fusion in scale-decision (we relied primarily on a single percentile channel)
Architecture: warm-pool seeding not large enough for the burst pattern observed; cold-start tail variance exposed
impact: Duration: ~18 minutes of degraded SLOs in us-east-1
Customer experience: increased p95/p99 generation latency; a small fraction of requests received 5xx responses during pod churn
Business: short-term error budget burn and 2 customer support tickets opened
detection: On-call telemetry: queue depth + pod CPU trending up while replicas did not increase
Ad hoc smoke tests showed >60% increase in tail latency under the same request mix
mitigation_during_incident: Increased HPA minReplicas for critical pools (owner: on-call)
Manually seeded 10 warm-pool nodes to reduce cold-start exposure
Rolled back the autoscaler aggregation change in production canary and then globally
Temporarily disabled KEDA approxQuantile mode via feature flag to revert to stable quantile mode

ENG/RELIABILITY: Expand warm-pool seeding policy and make warm-pool sizes workload-aware (owner: Priya Shah; estimate: 3; due: 2026-04-15)
ENG: Add end-to-end deterministic load tests that simulate heavy-tail cold-start patterns to CI (owner: QA Team; estimate: 5; due: 2026-04-08)
ENG: Add a canary gating policy that evaluates scale-decision stability under synthetic burst tests before promotion (owner: Maya Chen; estimate: 5; due: 2026-04-10)
DOCS: Update runbooks to include multi-signal checks and explicit warm-pool ramp playbook (owner: SRE Docs; estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-22)
